slides.text:
Shell completion lets the user press Tab to finish a command, a flag or a value. Cobra builds most of it for you: you only teach it the values it cannot know.

You will tune the built-in `completion` command, suggest fixed and computed values for arguments, and suggest values for flags.

The shell runs your program to ask for suggestions: it sends what is typed so far, and the program answers with a list and a hint about what the shell should do next.

The snippet is pseudo code.
slides.code:
shell:   app deploy st<Tab>
ask:     what can follow 'deploy st'?
program: staging + a hint for the shell
shell:   app deploy staging

slides.text: Names of subcommands and flags complete by themselves, and hidden ones stay out. Values are different: cobra cannot guess the formats of a flag or the tasks of a command, so you provide them.

intro.title: The completion command and fixed values

slides.text: A root command with subcommands gets a `completion` command for free. `app completion <shell>` prints a script for `bash`, `zsh`, `fish` or `powershell`, and each shell loads it in its own way. The snippet is shell, not Go.
slides.code:
source <(app completion bash)
app completion fish | source

slides.text: Three options on `root.CompletionOptions` tune it: `HiddenDefaultCmd` keeps the command out of the help, `DisableDefaultCmd` removes it, and `DisableDescriptions` drops the descriptions from the suggestions.

The scripts do not know your values: on every Tab they run the program through a hidden command, `__complete`, and print what it answers. You can call it by hand to see what the shell would get.

The snippet is pseudo code.
slides.code:
app __complete deploy s
  -> one suggestion per line
  -> a last line with the hint

slides.text: The list of values for an argument is the `ValidArgs` field of the command: the shell suggests them. A suggestion can carry a description after a tab character, and shells that can show descriptions print it.

slides.text:
When the values change, a fixed list is not enough. `ValidArgsFunction` runs every time Tab is pressed and returns the suggestions together with a directive.

The snippet is pseudo code.
slides.code:
complete(command, args typed, text):
    return suggestions, directive

slides.text:
The directive is a hint for the shell. The common ones:

- `ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp`: do not suggest file names
- `ShellCompDirectiveNoSpace`: do not add a space after the word
- `ShellCompDirectiveDefault`: let the shell suggest file names
- `ShellCompDirectiveError`: something failed, ignore the answer
Use the hidden command `__complete` from session 1 to see what the function answers without a shell: `app __complete deploy s` prints one suggestion per line, then the directive as a number.

slides.text: Flag names complete on their own, but their values do not. `RegisterFlagCompletionFunc` attaches a function to a flag by name. The function has the same signature and returns the same directives as for arguments.
Some flags take a file or a folder. Cobra has helpers that tell the shell which files to list, so no function is needed.

chunks.guide: The command prints the value of its flag. The completion function is already in the file.
Attach the function to the flag by its name.

notes.text: Prints the error and exits if there is one

chunks.text:
err := export.RegisterFlagCompletionFunc(
        "format", completeFormats,
    )
    cobra.CheckErr(err)

exercises.title: A ready-made list
exercises.guide: Suggest flag values from a ready-made list.

chunks.guide: No function needed: build one from a list and a directive. The command and its flag are already in the file.

notes.text: A ready-made function that returns this list

chunks.text:
err := report.RegisterFlagCompletionFunc(
        "level",
        cobra.FixedCompletions(
            []string{"debug", "info", "warn"},
            cobra.ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp,
        ),
    )
    cobra.CheckErr(err)
